audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove was described only as vague 'root setups' and 'E root', with nothing about how it actually works, and Vision of Empire was called his 'long-range Q poke' in content mid.
audit.why: Nevermove is 850 range on 12/11.5/11/10.5/10: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The root is on the RETURN pass — the danger arrives after the wave has already gone by, which is the exact opposite of how a player instinctively dodges it. It also has a shorter cooldown during Demonic Ascension. The long-range tool is Vision of Empire (W) at 5500 to 7500 by rank; Death's Hand is only 750.
audit.corrected: The return-pass root is now stated in tldr, loading, cooldowns, dosFull[2].d, whys[2], content early and spikes[2]. The two ranges are separated so the reader stops watching the wrong ability.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike said 'disengage and reset the fight when it starts' without ever saying why the fight does not just restart, and dosFull[2].d told the reader to wait for Swain to 'whiff Demonic Ascension'.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is a self-transform on 120s at 650 range — it cannot whiff. And 'This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions', which is precisely why leaving the circle beats trading inside it: with nobody in range the form ends.
audit.corrected: The 650 radius, the flat 120s, and the indefinite-while-draining clause are now written into winCon, cooldowns, breakdown.mid, report[5].t, whys[6], spikes[1] and spikes[3]. The whiff instruction is gone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The anti-heal interaction was flagged as missing and only appeared as a trailing clause in report[8] ('Add anti-heal early into his sustain') with no explanation anywhere else.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock: 'Swain's ravens collect Soul Fragments that heal him and permanently increase his maximum health.' The heal is not incidental — it is a permanent max-health gain, so a poke lane that never converts is a lane you slowly lose.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.feeding, breakdown.carry, ahead and content late, with Grievous Wounds named as a timing decision rather than a footnote.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit at all — defect-catalogue item 3.
audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: R 120s at 650, E 12s at rank 1 rooting on the return and shorter while transformed, Q 7s at rank 1 down to 3s at rank 5.

audit.whatIsWrong: Aurora's Q was called 'Twin Drift' in whys[0], spikes[0].text and content early, and Death's Hand was called a 'DoT' in whys[1] and spikes[0].text.
audit.why: 'Twin Drift' matches nothing in the kit file. Death's Hand is 'several bolts of eldritch power that pierce through enemies. Enemies hit take more damage for each bolt they are struck by' — a fan whose damage depends on how many bolts hit you, not damage over time. The positioning advice that follows from those two facts is completely different.
audit.corrected: Fabricated name removed (slot letter and the real 900 range used instead, since the kit file carries no Aurora ability names). Death's Hand described as a stacking fan, with the resulting instruction: never stand square to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] and spikes[2].text used 'Riftmaker/Shadowflame' against his 'Rod/Liandry scaling' while report[8] says Luden's into Sorcerer's, then Shadowflame and Rabadon's.
audit.why: Two builds on one page, and both slash forms are placeholder phrasing (defect item 7).
audit.corrected: Aligned to the page's own build; his side stated as the ult cooldown rather than guessed items.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string under a spirit-haste title and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string under 'Stand in his rotation during E cooldown'.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to answer their own titles.

audit.whatIsWrong: LEVEL CHART DISAGREEMENT. phases[0..6].side all read 'Skill' while content win[] reads [Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Swain, Aurora, Aurora].
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches win[] exactly, including the single Swain row at level 6, so the content layer and the packet agree and only phases[N].side dissents. The kit backs the shape: his 6 is a 650-range drain that holds while he keeps a champion in it, with Nevermove on a reduced cooldown throughout — one genuinely bad stage inside an otherwise favourable lane at 53.8%.
audit.corrected: All seven phases[N].side proposed as one atomic group to match win[]. phases[4].why is rewritten in the SAME proposal because that row now belongs to Swain and its old text described Aurora's zone winning the stage. content whys[4] already reads Swain-favouring, so the two layers now agree on that row for the first time.

edits.before: Between Worlds is your answer to his ultimate in teamfights — dash out the moment he tries to drain you and his damage output collapses since he has no other way to threaten squishies. edits.after: Between Worlds is your answer to his ultimate — leave the 650-unit circle the moment he transforms, because the form only lasts while he is draining a champion. notes: ALL THREE PACKET SUSPECTS ARE FALSE POSITIVES: 'His Demonic Ascension', 'Demonic Ascension's' and 'His Death's Hand' are the real ability names per the kit. I left the names alone and edited those fields only where the CLAIM attached to them was wrong. THE ROOT WORKS BACKWARDS AND THE PAGE NEVER SAID SO. Nevermove 'launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits' — the root lands on the RETURN pass, at 850 range, on 12s, with a reduced cooldown while he is ulted. A player who sidesteps the outgoing wave and then relaxes is exactly who this ability catches. That is now in seven fields and it is the single most valuable thing added to this page. RANGES WERE ATTACHED TO THE WRONG ABILITY: content mid warned about 'his long-range Q poke setups'. Death's Hand is 750. The long-range tool is Vision of Empire at 5500 to 7500 by rank. AN ULT THAT CANNOT WHIFF: dosFull[2].d told the reader to wait for Swain to 'whiff Demonic Ascension' — it is a self-transform. Replaced. NEW INTERACTION ADDED: Vision of Empire reveals champions it hits, and Aurora's W grants invisibility, so the W is not cover while his eye is on you. That is straight from Riot's text ('Champions hit are revealed') and it was nowhere on the page. FABRICATION KILLED: 'Twin Drift' for Aurora's Q, in whys[0], spikes[0].text and content early — sixth matchup in my slice with that invented name. CHART: phases[0..6].side all 'Skill' against win[] [Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Swain, Aurora, Aurora], which packet.levelChart matches exactly. Resolved to win[] as one atomic group, and phases[4].why rewritten in the same proposal so the level 6 row and its sentence both say Swain. BUILD CONFLICT: Riftmaker in whys[5] and spikes[2] against Luden's in report[8]; aligned to report[8].
unverified: The kit file tags Ravenous Flock with a percentHealth flag ('punishes HP stacking — armour alone is not the answer'), and the missing-interactions file turns that into 'Swain bypasses stacking resistances — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here'. Riot's own text says only that Soul Fragments 'heal him and permanently increase his maximum health' — that is health GAIN on his side, not percent-health damage on yours. Per the brief's rule I trusted the description and wrote nothing about resistances being invalidated. Only the anti-heal half of that missing-interaction entry was acted on.
